title: The "Total CPU Use" widget's configuration doesn't work
line: Clearing a sensor's label in the System Monitor widget's Sensors Details now hides that sensor's name, so "Total Usage" can be removed from the panel.
explanation: Sensor labels are set per sensor in the widget's Sensors Details page, but an empty label was dropped when saving, so clearing one just brought back the sensor name and "Total Usage" could not be removed from a panel. The faces also treated an empty label as missing, and the settings page edited its label map in place, so the sensor chips never showed a changed label until the widget was reloaded. An empty label is now saved and shown as no name in every face (the panel and the popup show only the value), its chip is greyed out in the settings, and typing the sensor's own name resets it to the default.

commits.message:
faces: Let an empty sensor label hide the sensor name

An empty sensor label was not saved and faces fell back to the sensor
name, so names like Total Usage could not be hidden. Save and honour
empty labels; typing the sensor's own name resets the label instead.

BUG: 501056

media.caption: Pure master: Total Usage label cleared in Sensors Details and applied; the label comes back and the panel still shows 'Total Usage'
With the fix, same steps: the cleared label is kept (chips greyed out) and the panel shows only the value, other names unchanged
Panel close-up on master after clearing the label
Panel close-up with the fix after clearing the label

review.text: Allowing empty sensor labels to hide sensor names (and fixing ConfigSensors.qml's in-place mutation of cfg_sensorLabels) is a much cleaner design than overloading Show Title, and the faces correctly switch from || to ?? so empty labels are honoured. However, changing Choices.qml's sensorLabelChanged signal to emit undefined on reset creates a hazard because SensorFaceController::setSensorLabels() writes it.value().toString() without checking QVariant validity/nullness, which would turn undefined/null into a saved empty label. On the UX side, repurposing an empty field from 'reset to default' to 'hide label' leaves users having to manually type the full localized sensor name verbatim to restore the default, and greying out cleared chips with disabledTextColor without explanation risks looking like a disabled sensor.
changes: In faces/SensorFaceController.cpp (setSensorLabels), ignore invalid or null QVariant entries (e.g. if (!it.value().isValid() || it.value().isNull()) continue;) so undefined/null values from QML callers cannot silently be saved as empty hidden labels.

In faces/import/Choices.qml, add an explicit reset-to-default control in the label editor so users do not have to type the exact sensor name verbatim to undo a custom or cleared label, and clarify cleared chips (e.g. via tooltip) so disabledTextColor is not mistaken for a disabled sensor.
In faces/facepackages/piechart/contents/ui/UsedTotalDisplay.qml, hide usedLabel/totalLabel when text.length === 0 so intentionally empty labels do not take up layout space.

reviews.text: Addresses the reporter's main ask (remove the 'Total Usage' text in the panel) in libksysguard: empty labels are now saved and honoured with ?? across all faces, the settings chip shows the cleared state, and typing the sensor name resets it, which fixes the earlier in-place map mutation that kept chips stale. The cores/threads half is already fixed by ksystemstats f054defeba, and the Show Title checkbox is left alone (the compact text-only face never shows a title), which is a reasonable scope. Media show the panel with only the value and other sensors unchanged. The reset-by-typing-the-name flow is a bit hidden, but the placeholder text makes it workable.
